subject.title: [Bug]: Fallback model does not report progress correctly during long tasks

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee identical source-channel intermediate progress for successful fallback model attempts, including cross-provider fallbacks with different streaming and tool-progress capabilities?
rationale: The report spans fallback routing, provider behavior, and channel-visible progress, so maintainers need to set the shared product contract before a repair chooses between strict parity, documented degraded behavior, or a broader delivery-contract effort.

options.title: Guarantee parity in core
options.body: Treat fallback attempts as the same progress contract as primary attempts and fix the shared fallback/progress plumbing with focused tests.

options.title: Document degraded providers
options.body: Guarantee only diagnostic/final fallback notices where a provider cannot stream comparable intermediate progress, and document the limitation.

options.title: Fold into delivery contract
options.body: Track this under the broader channel delivery semantics work if maintainers want one project to own fallback visibility across final and intermediate messages.

recommendation.title: Guarantee parity in core
recommendation.body: Treat fallback attempts as the same progress contract as primary attempts and fix the shared fallback/progress plumbing with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the central model fallback mechanism and is the strongest history signal for setting the fallback behavior contract.
